Those three are the whole changed-by-design surface this re-review judges; the eleven others are production the S2 and S3 craft turns wrote and are not this subject.

The delta over the approved S2 bytes is additive everywhere it touches an S2 observation. argv git diff --numstat 6314c32 HEAD -- crates/foundry-acceptance/, exit 0: 30 added and 0 removed in the steps file, 181 added and 0 removed in the support file, 184 added and 2 removed in the feature file. So no step binding and no support helper that any S2 scenario calls was changed or removed - a file with zero deleted lines cannot have weakened one. The two removed feature lines are the only removal in the slice's oracle: two comment lines above the healthy-key scenario, replaced by three comment lines. They are not executable, the first three lines of that comment are untouched, and the replacement states the stale-tab motivation of the half S3 appended rather than withdrawing anything the S2 comment claimed. The feature diff holds exactly two hunks; every other S2 scenario of this oracle is byte-identical to the approved revision, and all seven S2 acceptance-row titles are still present in the file, at lines 1202, 1234, 1254, 1275, 1299, 1326 and 1349.

The one S2 scenario S3 extended keeps its whole approved observation, in its approved order, and the appended half cannot mask an S2 regression. At feature lines 1349-1368 the S2 half stands unchanged first: the healthy page read, Replace offered, no way to start over offered, then the start over GET answered this Foundry's integrations page, the stored key and the Activity as they were, and Canzan Labs' saved Slack connection still opening. The appended half follows it: a post to the same address, the same answer, the same preservation pair, the absence of "Secrets key generated.", the saved connection and the saved Slack app unchanged. Because a cucumber scenario stops at its first failing step, a step appended after an observation can only fail the scenario, never satisfy it - the appended half runs only on a scenario whose S2 half has already passed. The cited run at 9a9908a shows exactly that execution order: log lines 502-516 mark every S2 step of this scenario passed, and the first failure of the scenario is the appended post step, Defined tests/features/instance-integration-setup.feature:1362. The S2 observations of the scenario were therefore still executed and still held after the extension.

Reuse of the recorded S2 semantic RED, with the current comparison that justifies it and no new execution claimed. The RED of this slice is observation R3 of this record, measured at revision 6314c32: 21 scenarios, 12 passed and 9 failed, 304 steps, 0 parsing and 0 hook errors, lane exit 101, nine semantic failures on the absent Start over offer, the absent live-server sentence and the start-over GET answering 404. The recorded RED therefore remains the RED of these same S2 observations at this commit. Implementation GREEN is a completion obligation of this value, not a pre-craft prerequisite, and this round invents no second RED.

The log ends at that summary. Among those 29 are the seven S2 scenarios, the healthy-key one at log line 491 with both halves passing. So every S2 observation this record approved is executable, collected and holding at the commit under review; nothing in the S3 delta left an S2 row unselected, unmatched or silently skipped.

The steps delta adds six bindings and removes none: typing a confirmation and choosing Start over on the start over page, having started over with a new secrets key, the stored key being one this Foundry opens, the workspace page reading no connection as connected, the second server having said nothing for a minute, and the second server speaking again. The S3 round observes it: the healthy-key scenario now carries that post with the preservation pair, the absent "Secrets key generated." and the saved Slack app unchanged, which is the row the finding's remediation named, placed in the scenario that already owns the law instead of in a new one.
